The core methodological framework combines two key steps: first, estimating win probability \( P(Win|PS) \) through a non-parametric mapping of historical outcomes at given spreads, bypassing distributional assumptions. This step leverages the empirical frequency of wins at specific spreads, assuming stationarity and bookmaker accuracy. Second, computing expected value \( EV \) using the maximum payout across a panel of 16 bookmakers, which introduces a robustness check against mispricing. The algorithm then applies two thresholds: \( \varepsilon \) to ensure the probability is near 0.5 (indicating inefficiency), and \( \tau \) to ensure \( EV > 0 \). These thresholds define a dual regime where only high-confidence, positive-EV bets are selected. Failure modes include overfitting due to in-sample hyperparameter tuning, stale data, and lack of NBBO enforcement. The model’s strength lies in its portability across sports, but requires GSE-grade hardening for real-time application.
